How do I get to Koh Samui? | Fly direct to Samui Airport (USM) with Bangkok Airways, about 1 h 05 min from Bangkok Suvarnabhumi with 20–25 flights a day and fares of roughly 2,800–6,800 THB one way. The cheaper alternative is a low-cost flight to Surat Thani plus a coach and ferry (5–7 hours, about 1,500–3,000 THB all-in), or the night train and ferry (15–17 hours).
~What is the best time to visit Koh Samui? | February to April has the driest weather and calmest sea, which is ideal for Ang Thong and island trips. May to September is also good because Samui is sheltered from the south-west monsoon. October to December is the rainy season, with November the wettest month at about 445 mm.
Where should I stay on Koh Samui for a first visit? | Chaweng, for the widest choice of restaurants and hotels and a 10–15 minute ride from the airport. If you want quiet with Chaweng close by, choose Chaweng Noi or Choeng Mon; for food and atmosphere, Bophut and Fisherman's Village.
~How many days do I need on Koh Samui? | Five to seven days lets you do a round-island loop, two boat trips (Ang Thong or Pig Island, plus Koh Tao) and a slow beach or spa day. Three days covers the highlights; ten days adds Koh Phangan and an Ang Thong overnight.
~Do I need a visa for Thailand in 2026? | Citizens of 60 countries and territories, including the UK, US, Canada, Australia and all EU states, get 30 days visa-free since 15 September 2026, extendable once by up to 30 days at the Samui immigration office in Maenam for 1,900 THB. Everyone must also file the free TDAC arrival card online within 3 days before arrival.
~Is Ang Thong Marine Park open in November? | No. The park closes every year from 1 November to 15 December and reopens on 16 December. During the closure we recommend the Pig Island speedboat tour (1,450 THB), which runs all year, or the Koh Tao and Koh Nang Yuan day trip (2,200 THB), sea permitting.
Is Koh Samui expensive? | It is the most expensive Gulf island, mainly because of flights and resorts, but it can still be done cheaply. Our 2026 estimates are about 1,500–2,500 THB per person per day on a budget, 4,000–7,000 THB mid-range and 15,000 THB or more for luxury, excluding flights.
Do I need cash on Koh Samui? | Yes, some. Cards work in malls, hotels, 7-Eleven and most restaurants, but street food, songthaews, many taxis and the island fees on boat trips (Ang Thong 300 THB, Koh Nang Yuan 250 THB, Koh Madsum about 50 THB) are cash only. Foreign-card ATM fees are 220–250 THB per withdrawal, or 150 THB at AEON machines.
Is Koh Samui safe for tourists? | Generally yes; the real risks are road accidents on rented scooters and rip currents. Ride with a helmet and an International Driving Permit, stay out of the sea when red flags fly (Chaweng and Lamai, October to December), and treat any box jellyfish sting with vinegar for at least 30 seconds. Emergency numbers: Tourist Police 1155, ambulance 1669.
Does Grab work on Koh Samui? | Yes, but coverage is thinner than in Bangkok: best in Chaweng, Bophut and Lamai, weaker on the west coast, with surges in rain. Short hops cost about 80–120 THB and airport runs 300–600 THB; at the airport you meet the driver outside the pickup lane.
Can I visit Koh Phangan or Koh Tao in a day from Samui? | Yes. Koh Phangan is 20–50 minutes by boat, so a day trip by ferry or private speedboat is easy. Koh Tao is 1 h 30–2 h each way; our Koh Tao and Koh Nang Yuan speedboat tour (2,200 THB, about 8–9 hours) is the simplest way to see it in a day.
What is your cancellation policy for Koh Samui tours? | Day tours: full refund 48 hours or more before departure, 50% at 24–48 hours, none under 24 hours or for a no-show. Ang Thong tours: full refund 48 hours or more before, none under 48 hours. If we cancel for weather or sea safety, you choose a full refund or a new date.
